title: Fred Ramsey and how the chapters were assigned
summary: Ramsey's job at Harcourt and tastes, and why Russell was asked to write on boogie woogie, Armstrong and New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Now Ramsey was working for the Harcourt at this time.
Yeah, he was actually working for Harcourt Grace until at least sometime after the book came out, I guess.
Did he get interested in jazz when he was working at Harcourt?

Or had he always been interested? He'd probably been interested in, he was another guy from Princeton and I don't know, the first time I met him was through the Hot Record Exchange. He came up either to buy some records or to trade records.
Do you remember what he was interested in? What did it have been?
Just everything. He liked New Orleans especially too.

Yeah, Louie and Oliver and Bessie Smith just everybody that I sort of liked and including some of the Boogie Woogie pianists. Medlux Lewis was already in New York at that time came there in the fall of 38. No, that's right Medlux hadn't gotten to New York when it started on Jazzman. But I'd written an article on Boogie Woogie for Panacea's magazine which had come out oh, several months before we started on Jazzman and Ramsey had read that and liked the article so that's why he asked me to write an article on Boogie Woogie and he knew I was a Louis Armstrong fanatic and to write that chapter and then the first chapter the so-called New Orleans music chapter but Ramsey was interested in all sorts of jazz I'd say often went down to Nixon altars where he knew a lot of Chicago guys didn't know them intimately neither did I I used to see people like Pee Wee and I never did really talk to Condon more in just a few maybe remarks here and there in my life he would hardly remember me if he'd seen me in late years he wouldn't have known my name I don't believe but we all did go to Knicks quite often so anyway Ramsey did that and I know I got mad about a couple of things let's see one thing which is now even the musicians here unfortunately have read the book here too and some of them think the old hymn that they used isn't I guess it's a hymn is it or not Flea is a Bird
